articles.title: Mets lose to Astros despite strong start from Lindor and Soto
articles.summary: The offense was out-hit, and the bullpen could not keep things close during this rubber game loss.
articles.body:
The Mets struggled in multiple facets again in their loss to the Astros 6-3. Despite a decent outing from Zac Thornton, the Mets' bullpen could not hang on to the fragile lead they were given, and the offense had no response.

On his third pitch in the first inning, Thornton gave up a lead-off home run to Jeremy Peña. After striking out the next two hitters, Thornton allowed a single to Jose Altuve on a line drive into center field, but recovered when Christian Walker grounded into a force out for the third out. The Mets punched back quickly against Astros' rookie pitcher Ethan Pecko. Francisco Lindor led off with a home run on a full count, and Juan Soto followed with another dinger on the first pitch he saw. With no outs recorded, Bo Bichette smacked a ground ball into right field for a single. Unfortunately, the next three Mets batters went down in order to set the tone for the rest of the game. Nevertheless, after the first inning, the score was Mets 2, Astros 1.

With one out in the top of the second inning, Thornton hit Yainer Diaz with a pitch. After another out, Nick Allen bunted so softly that it took a minute for Marcus Semien to get to the ball and throw to first. By the time he did, Allen was safe, as was Diaz at second. Peña followed with an RBI single into center field that scored Diaz and moved Allen to third base. Fortunately, Yordan Alvarez flied out to mitigate the damage with the game tied. The Mets had no answers in the bottom of the inning, and the score remained 2-2.

Despite allowing a single to Walker at the top of the third, Thornton kept the Astros' hitters from scoring again. At the top of the fourth, the Astros' hitters continued to drive up Thornton's pitch count, and with two outs, Allen drove a double into the left-field corner. Peña came to the plate next, but fortunately this time he grounded out to Lindor at short. Thornton worked a 1-2-3 fifth inning, which was his last.

The Mets' offense was quiet for several innings until A.J. Ewing walked in the bottom of the fifth. He stole second base, and when Diaz's throw bounced past Peña, Ewing advanced to third as well. Marcus Semien walked to bring up Luis Torrens. Torrens grounded into a double play for the first two outs, but Ewing scored. Francisco Lindor grounded out to end the fifth inning, but the Mets were ahead 3-2.

Jonathan Pintaro replaced Thornton at the top of the sixth inning. After allowing a two-out double to right field from Diaz, Pintaro gave up a 2-run home run to pinch-hitter LaMonte Wade Jr, also in right field. Allen looped a single into center field after the homer to keep the rally going briefly, until Peña struck out to end the half. At the bottom of the sixth, Bichette smacked a double into center field for the Mets' first hit since the first inning. However, the Mets' lineup could not find any other momentum, and the inning ended with an Astros' lead, 4-3.

At the top of the seventh, Jefry Yan came in to pitch. After the first out, he issued a four-pitch walk to Isaac Paredes, then allowed a single to Altuve by deflecting a comebacker off his glove. Yan followed this up by hitting Walker with a pitch to load the bases. Daulton Varsho grounded out to first base, but Paredes scored on the play. Jared Young's subsequent throw to home was very wide, allowing Altuve and Walker to score as well. Diaz struck out for the third out, but the score was now Astros 6, Mets 3.

Austin Warren replaced Yan at the top of the eighth and retired the batters in order. With one out, Soto and Bichette both walked at the bottom of the eighth. The Astros opted to swap Bryan Abreu for Steven Okert, a lefty, on the mound at this point. The gambit worked when Okert retired Carson Benge to strand the runners and end the eighth-inning threat.

Chris Devenski pitched the ninth inning for the Mets and worked a 1-2-3 inning as well against his former team. After a delay to work on the mound, Josh Hader retired the first two batters he saw. Ewing doubled on a line drive to center field, but Semien flied out to end the game with an Astros win, 6-3.

The Mets travel to St. Petersburg to start a new series against the Tampa Bay Rays tomorrow. Robert Stock will face Ian Seymour, and first pitch is scheduled for 6:40 PM.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler wins second FedEx Cup title: Golf roundup
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler joined golf royalty as the third player to win multiple FedEx Cup championships.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — Scottie Scheffler has joined elite company.

Tiger Woods. Rory McIlroy. Scheffler. That's it. That's the list.

Scheffler joined golf royalty as the only players to win multiple FedEx Cup championships when he came from behind to capture the Tour Championship in the finale of the FedEx Cup playoffs Sunday, Aug. 30 at East Lake Golf Club.

Scheffler outdueled Norway's Viktor Hovland, who was also trying to join the multiple-Tour Championships club.

Scheffler, the world's No. 1 player and point standings leader, shot a 4-under-par 66 to finish 16-under 264, three shots ahead of Hovland. It was the second Tour Championship victory in three years for Scheffler, who won in 2024.

Hovland, the 2023 champion, couldn't hold a one-stroke lead heading into the final round. He shot 2-over to finish alone in second at 13 under.

McIlroy won the FedEx Cup three times (2016, 2019, 2022) and Woods twice (2007, 2009).

Scheffler overtook Woods for the top spot on the PGA Tour's career money list. With the $10 million first prize, Scheffler now stands at the top with $130,390,661. Woods held the top spot with $120,999,166.

Simply, Scheffler took the championship by matching the low round of the day.

Back and forth they battled, with Scheffler playing two groups ahead. Hovland, at 15 under, led Scheffler by three strokes going into the final round.

Scheffler started strong by hitting his tee shot on the par-3 second to two inches. The birdie moved him one and two strokes behind Ryan Gerard and Hovland, respectively, before the leaders even teed off. Scheffler then birdied the fourth to tie for the lead with Hovland at 14 under, after the first-round leader bogeyed his opening hole. Gerard double-bogeyed the opening hole to fall behind.

Scheffler bogeyed the seventh but birdied the eighth to move back to 14 under and tied with Hovland.

Hovland birdied the eighth to move back to 15 under and retake the solo lead. Scheffler birdied the 10th to force another tie, then made a 5-footer for birdie at the 13th to move to 16 under and take the solo lead for the first time. He gave the lead back with a bogey on the 14th after a drive in the rough.

Hovland dropped back behind Scheffler with a bogey on the 13th, also following a drive in the rough.

The lead was two after Scheffler birdied the 16th, from the fairway bunker, to return to 16 under.

While Scheffler was playing the 18th, Hovland bogeyed the 17th to fall three shots back. He overshot the green from 103 yards with a lob wedge. Scheffler parred the 18th, but at that point had the comfortable lead with one hole to play. Hovland went on to par the 18th.

No one else really challenged Scheffler and Hovland. Of the others in the final three pairings: Gerard shot 2-over 72 and finished third at 12 under. Adam Scott of Australia also shot 72 and finished 10 under, tied for 11th.

Chris Gotterup and Sweden's Ludvig Aberg each carded a 1-over 71 and finished tied for fourth at 11 under along with McIlroy (69).

They were joined by Englishman Alex Fitzpatrick (66), Jacob Bridgeman (68), Australian Min Woo Lee (68) and Russell Henley (68).

Scheffler moves closer to the Player of the Year award with his third win, including two in the playoffs, and 10 top-3 finishes.

Yin wins for first time since 2024 at FM Championship

China's Ruoning Yin fought off a challenge by South Korea's Hyo Joo Kim and captured the FM Championship by two strokes on at TPC Boston in Norton, Mass.

Yin, 23, carded a 2-under-par 70 and finished with a 14-under total of 274 to win for the sixth time on tour.

Kim, who grabbed the lead and got to 13 under by birdieing holes Nos. 7, 9 and 10, bogeyed the 16th hole and recorded a 1-under 71 to finish solo second at 12 under.

Allisen Corpuz (11 under) and Rose Zhang (10 under) tied for the low round of the day at 4-under 68. Corpuz, who was tied for the lead after two rounds, finished alone in third place, while Zhang tied for fourth with South Korea's Sei Young Kim (73).

Yin, Hyo Joo Kim and Sei Young Kim battled all day in the final group and each held a lead on the back nine.

Sei Young Kim chipped in for a birdie 2 on the par-3 11th to get to 14 under, but took a double-bogey 7 on the ensuing hole and two more bogeys on Nos. 13 and 14 to fall out of contention.

Yin rolled in a 25-foot birdie putt on the par-5 12th hole to tie Hyo Joo Kim at 13 under.

But Hyo Joo Kim suffered a three-putt bogey on the par-3 16th hole, misfiring from 9 feet away for par.

Both players parred No. 17 and Yin finished off her first win of the year with a birdie on the 72nd hole. Yin's last win occurred at the Maybank Championship in October 2024.

Top-ranked Nelly Korda shot a 1-over 73 and tied for 50th place at 1 over for the week.

Sweden's Anna Nordqvist wrapped up her final event on the LPGA Tour by tying for 38th at 1 under. The 39-year-old three-time major champion will captain the European team at the Solheim Cup next month.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills 53-man roster 2026: Here's who made the team
articles.summary: Here is the Buffalo Bills' initial 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season, with the full list of players by position.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have their initial roster for the 2026 NFL season.

Buffalo reduced its roster to 53 players ahead of Sunday's NFL deadline after three preseason games and more than a month of training camp.

The roster still could change before the Bills open the regular season Sept. 13 against the Houston Texans . Waiver claims will be processed Monday, while Buffalo can also make additional signings and injured-reserve moves.

Here's the Bills' initial 53-man roster:

D.J. Moore, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer, Skyler Bell

Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox, Jackson Hawes, Keleki Latu

Dion Dawkins, Spencer Brown, Tylan Grable, Jude Bowry

O'Cyrus Torrence, Alec Anderson, Austin Corbett, Ar'maj Reed-Adams

Bradley Chubb, Greg Rousseau, Michael Hoecht, T.J. Parker, Javon Solomon, Mike Danna

Deone Walker, Landon Jackson, T.J. Sanders, Greg Gaines, Zane Durant, DeWayne Carter

Terrel Bernard, Dorian Williams, Kaleb Elarms-Orr, Joe Andreessen

Christian Benford, Maxwell Hairston, Dee Alford, Davison Igbinosun, Jordan Hancock

Cole Bishop, C.J. Gardner-Johnson, Damar Hamlin, Jalon Kilgore, Sam Franklin Jr.

Reserve/Non-Football Injury: CB Dorian Strong

Can the Bills' 53-man roster still change?

Yes. This is Buffalo's initial 53-man roster.

NFL teams can submit waiver claims through 1 p.m. Monday, and the Bills can add players who were released by other teams. Buffalo also can make additional injured-reserve moves after the initial roster is established.

The Bills will begin assembling their practice squad Monday after the waiver process is completed.

articles.title: Cincinnati Bengals 53-man roster: Here's who made the team
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals revealed the first 53-man roster of the 2026 season. Here's who made the cut.
articles.body:
The team publicly announced its cuts and other roster designations moments after the Aug. 30 6 p.m. deadline.

Bengals head coach Zac Taylor on Aug. 28 said he expected the weekend to be a tense time of trimming down the roster because of the team's apparent depth. Here's what the team landed on for its initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season.

The Bengals terminated four contracts and waived 30 players as part of reached their initial 53-man roster. The team on Aug. 31 expects to announce its 16-player practice squad.

Two players were placed on injured reserve.

Cincinnati should look similar in 2026 on the offensive side in terms of starters, although there was noteworthy turnover in some of the depth spots.

Defensively, Dexter Lawrence headlined some noticeable roster churn resulting from the team's work in offseason free agency and in the NFL Draft.

All told, Cincinnati rostered two quarterbacks, six wide receivers, three running backs, five tight ends, nine offensive linemen, 11 defensive lineman, 10 defensive backs, four linebackers and three specialists.

articles.title: Steelers make rare decision with 4 QBs on 53-man roster for 2026
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers made the rare decision to carry four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The final roster cuts have arrived, which means there's no more speculating as to what the Pittsburgh Steelers will do with their quarterback room.

On NFL roster cutdown day, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Steelers indeed plan to keep four quarterbacks on their 53-man squad: Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard , and Drew Allar.

Four-man quarterback rooms are rare when it comes to 53-man rosters, which is why many assumed the loser of the QB2 battle between Rudolph and Howard would get a one-way ticket out of Pittsburgh. But the Steelers apparently erred on the side of caution, opting to keep two veterans and two young quarterbacks heading into the 2026 season.

Surprisingly enough, the Steelers aren't the only AFC North team to bring four quarterbacks onto their roster, as the Cleveland Browns are expected to keep Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel (IR), and rookie Taylen Green in their 2026 quarterback room.

With the Steelers set to keep four quarterbacks, other positions will unfortunately see their depth tested, as evidenced by the recent releases of fan-favorite linebacker Elandon Roberts and 32-year-old veteran defensive lineman Dean Lowry.

For up-to-date Steelers coverage, including any roster news and injury updates, follow us on X @TheSteelersWire and give our Facebook page a like.

articles.title: Texans to place WR Tank Dell on injured reserve to begin 2026 season
articles.summary: WR Tank Dell addresses the media for the first time since his gruesome knee injury that caused him to miss the 2025 season.
articles.body:
Finally, the Houston Texans have revealed their plans for wide receiver Tank Dell headed into the 2026 NFL season.

According to multiple reports, the Texans have placed Dell on the injured reserve to begin the season. The speedster will miss the first four games of the season, but will be eligible to return Oct. 11 against the Tennessee Titans at Reliant Stadium.

Dell tore his ACL, MCL and LCL, along with dislocating his kneecap and suffering significant meniscus damage, which required multiple surgeries and forced him to miss the entire 2025 season while rehabbing. For 18 months, fans pondered if the former third-round pick would ever return to full form.

Fast-forward to this training camp and Dell was back at practice in a limited role.

As much as the physical recovery was challenging, Dell mentioned the internal struggle as a focal issue, too.

"I'll say mentally, it's just about trusting that the work you put in prior to going out there to do those things," Dell said avout his recovery last month. "Prior to going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the training staff and what they had set out for me so that when I got out here I wasn't scared and I was talking to my doctor and I was just asking him questions and he was just telling me to let loose, trust it and be you because it's 100% stable. When he told me that, I just came out and was putting my foot in the ground. I didn't care about it, I tried not to think about it, because during your process the mental aspect of it is the hardest thing you have to get over. If I went out there iffy about what I'm doing, then I probably would never be able to come back to what I want to be. I was just out there, just trusting it, putting my foot in the ground, trying to be explosive and it's working in my favor."

Over his two active seasons with the Texans, Dell has caught 98 passes for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns. He's thankful for the team's patience and belief in his recovery, but he's now ready to be back after a short stint on IR.

Right now, the Texans only have five receivers on the active roster: Nico Collins, Jaylin Noel, Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson and Jared Wayne.

articles.title: Full list of Patriots moves at the NFL roster deadline
articles.summary: The Patriots made 42 total transactions ahead of the NFL roster cutdown deadline.
articles.body:
Coming out of their preseason finale and entering cutdown weekend, the New England Patriots had 91 players on their roster. Accordingly, they and their players were in for a few busy days: before Sunday's roster cutdown deadline, they needed to make at least 38 moves to get below the 53-player threshold mandated by the NFL.

In actuality, they made 42. The first 19 of those moves happened on Saturday, as did one that actually added a player to the mix . The rest — a total of 22 additional transitions, as charted by our Patriots roster cuts tracker — took place on Sunday.

The full list, split in different categories for easier digestion, looks as follows.

Players with less than four years of accrued experience are subject to waivers. This means that the following 31 will first have to pass through the waiver wire, where they might get claimed by any NFL team, before entering the open market.

The lion's share of cuts made over the weekend were of the waiver variety. As noted above, all of the players listed here are now subject to being claimed by other clubs before they could potentially return to the Patriots practice squad or, in the case of Jam Miller and Eric Butler, revert to injured reserve.

As for the list itself, it mostly includes depth players whose odds of making the 53-man roster were slim to begin with. The few names worth pointing out include running backs Lan Larison and Jam Miller, who are candidates to return should they clear waivers, as well as linebacker Chad Muma. Safety John Saunders Jr. also looked like a roster-worthy player but ultimately was made obsolete due to the trade acquisition of Jaylen Reed.

The following players were let go as vested veterans, meaning that the do not have to pass through waivers. They become free agents right away, meaning that they can sign with any team now.

The biggest surprise among the veterans being let go by the Patriots over the weekend was Kindle Vildor. The 2020 fifth-round draft choice, who joined the team in free agency this offseason, looked like a potential fifth cornerback at times during training camp. However, he ultimately was cut in favor of two rookies, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada.

Patriots players placed on reserve lists

The players listed here were all sent to reserve lists ahead of the roster cutdown deadline. All three of the names listed here are eligible to return.

Marcus Bryant will open the season on injured reserve with a designation to return. He will have to sit out at least the first four weeks of the regular season, as will Harold Landry and Brenden Schooler, whose statuses on the physically unable to perform and non-football injury/illness lists were changed from "active" to "reserve" on Sunday.

Not on this list yet are the aforementioned Jam Miller and Eric Butler, who were waived with an injury designation over the weekend. They will revert to New England's IR list once they make it through the waiver wire unclaimed.

While roster cuts made up the vast majority of moves this weekend, the Patriots also brought in some talent through the trade market.

The Patriots sent a 2028 seventh-round draft pick to the Cardinals to acquire Corey Kiner and did a late-round pick exchange with the Vikings to bring in Walter Rouse. Both moves are of the low-cost variety and effectively allow the team to jump the waiver wire: instead of waiting for Kiner or Rouse to remain unclaimed until it is their turn at No. 31, the Patriots secured their rights via trade.

articles.title: Titans roster announced for 2026 season after NFL cut day
articles.summary: Here's the full list of 53 players who've made the Tennessee Titans' active roster coming out of NFL cut day before the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans have announced their initial 53-man roster ahead of the start of the 2026 NFL season , though plenty is still subject to change.

The Titans trimmed their active roster down to 53 players from the 91 men it stood at throughout training camp on Aug. 30 in accordance with the NFL deadline. Most prominently, the Titans parted ways with quarterback Will Levis , a one-time starter who'd been groomed to be the Titans' quarterback of the future in 2023-24 before being benched and replaced. Other prominent players who didn't make the cut for the Titans include guard Cordell Volson, wide receiver K.J. Osborn and DE Malik Herring.

Just because the Titans are at 53 players now doesn't mean the roster is set in stone. The Titans still sit at No. 4 in the waiver order and can put in claims to pick up waiver-eligible players who were released on Aug. 30. The deadline to put in claims is noon CT on Aug. 31, and anyone who the Titans are awarded via waivers will have to be signed directly to the active roster.

articles.title: Bears finalize initial 53-man roster, cut LB Jack Sanborn, WR Kaden Davis: reactions
articles.summary: What you see today when it comes to the Bears’ 53-man roster will be different as soon as tomorrow. And it will change again. Then again and again … and...
articles.body:
What you see today when it comes to the Bears ' 53-man roster will be different as soon as tomorrow. And it will change again.

Things are always fluid with the construction of NFL rosters – especially when you're a young team like the Bears with a coaching staff entering its second season together.

With that said, there's still plenty you can glean from the team's initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season, whether it's certain strengths, glaring weaknesses or surprise decisions.

Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum

Adam Jahns: The Bears have one of the best young starters in the league, one of the best young backups in the league and one of the most experienced mentors in the league. Not bad at all. The Bears used to dream about QB rooms like they have right now under head coach Ben Johnson .

Mark Carman: One year ago things were "fra-gee-lay" between Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams behind the scenes. Now they are on the same track, being supported by Tyson Bagent, who many, including Ben Johnson, believe should be a starter in the league. Keeping Case Keenum around for his mentorship was a solid choice as well.

Greg Braggs Jr.: The starter is on the cover of Madden, Ben Johnson thinks the backup is a top-32 QB in the league and the third-string is better than the Vikings' starter. QB coach J.T. Barrett is probably better than half the QBs in my lifetime. What a room.

D'Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, Roschon Johnson

Jahns: With a roster spot to secure, Johnson had arguably the best outing of his career against the Titans: 46 offensive snaps, 15 carries, 52 yards, a touchdown, two catches, 11 yards. He also excelled in pass protection. Rookie receiver Zavion Thomas doesn't get to show his speed on his 97-yard touchdown catch without Johnson sliding over to pick up a blitzer.

Patrick Norton : Johnson making the roster shouldn't come as a shock to anybody. He's a valuable special-teamer and well-liked within the locker room despite his lacking offensive contributions. Don't be surprised to see Salvon Ahmed brought back to the practice squad. He could get some action with a game-day elevation to the active roster if Kyle Monangai is unable to go in Week 1 after hyperextending his knee earlier in the preseason.

Carman: One of the key question marks the Bears have entering the season is the health of Monangai. There is a significant drop-off between Monangai and Johnson. Ben Johnson might have to rely on D'Andre Swift a little more than he would like in the early going. Swift has looked up to the task, primed for perhaps his best season yet vying for a new contract.

Braggs: If Colston Loveland didn't exist, D'Andre Swift would probably be the Camp MVP this year. He has looked really good. I would give my life for Kyle Monangai. But Roschon Johnson making this team surprised me. Was not expecting that. Hey, if you live up to the challenge put by Ben, that's all right by me.

Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Kalif Raymond, Zavion Thomas, Jahdae Walker

Adam Hoge: This is the most talent the Bears have had at wide receiver since the Brandon Marshall-Alshon Jeffery days, and this group probably has a higher overall ceiling. But it is a young group, so the continued development of Odunze, Burden, Thomas and Walker throughout the season will be interesting to watch. Raymond already has had a big impact as the veteran in the room, but how many catches will he actually have in the regular season?

Norton : It's not worth acting surprised for a few hours that Kaden Davis didn't make the initial roster. The shock would come if he isn't invited back to the practice squad — or even the active roster once safety Coby Bryant is placed on injured reserve.

Carman: Who will step up and take the No. 1 receiver spot? The gambling markets are betting on Burden, as is Burden, who is his usual confident self. Thomas had a stellar end to the preseason and Walker is likely to make a jump as well. Can Odunze stay healthy and be the guy the Bears drafted him to be?

Braggs: Burden is in for a monster year. But if anybody's selling stock on Odunze, I'll buy it. Raymond may end up being the most crucial pickup of the entire offseason if the clear mentorship he's shown this summer pays off the way I think it will. Walker continues to intrigue me with star potential. The dude is a psycho.

Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, Sam Roush, Hayden Large

Norton : Hayden Large was one of the UDFAs that ALLCITY draft expert Fran Duffy considered a challenger for the initial roster back in April. Versatile as a blocking threat out of the backfield, he's a piece Ben Johnson should enjoy deploying.

Carman: The biggest sure thing on the roster is this room. Loveland becoming the best tight end in football is on the table. He will get a chance to do it as Caleb seems more comfortable with him than anyone else. Roush is not ready yet, but it seems like he will contribute. Kmet is Mr. Reliable and deserves to play on a winner as much as anyone in the Bears locker room.

Braggs: Colston Loveland has a chance to be one of the best players in the NFL. End scene.

Tackles: Darnell Wright, Braxton Jones, Theo Benedet, Ozzy Trapilo

Interior: Joe Thuney, Jonah Jackson, Garrett Bradbury, Logan Jones, Luke Newman, Jordan McFadden

Hoge : The bad news is that the Bears' wide-open left tackle competition didn't really work, but the good news is that Jones – once again the winner by default – is healthier than he was a year ago when he struggled to get through full games. The even better news is that Trapilo is coming. I wouldn't be shocked if he gets involved in team drills this week.

Carman: It is now or never for Braxton Jones, who is getting an opportunity that very few thought he would get. It feels like the Bears are holding on for Ozzy Trapilo but when will that be? Jones seemed very confident in his return to play early in camp before getting hurt. How far did that set him back? Meanwhile, Bradbury was not pushed at all by Jones early, but Jones is at least starting to find his way.

Braggs: When Cole Kmet says the transition at center has been seamless from Drew Dalman to Bradbury, I believe him. That is the most important storyline for the offensive line this offseason, of which there were many. They proved last year they can maneuver around a murky left tackle situation, and that was last year with an offense less prepared. Not worried about that unit one bit. Pretty nice, huh?

Edge: Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Dayo Odeyingbo, Jamree Kromah, Daniel Hardy

Interior: Grady Jarrett, Kentavius Street, Neville Gallimore, Jordan van den Berg, Jayden Loving

Jahns : The Bears' decision to trade Gervon Dexter Sr. is rooted in the past and the future. He was drafted in the second round in 2023 to fill a role in former coach Matt Eberflus' defense – and he was in the final year of his contract. A second contract with the Bears was unlikely.

Dexter was a solid but not a sensational player. His role and importance appeared to be diminishing during training camp, though. Street and van den Berg started to rotate in with the first team weeks ago. It didn't stop, either.

Instead, Loving – an undrafted rookie – also started to impress more and more.

Hoge : This is a much better interior group than the Bears had last year, with a solid group of veterans mixed in with two rookies who are already outperforming their draft status.

But the outside pass rush remains eerily similar to last year, especially because Booker is dealing with an injury again.

Braggs: Ben Johnson is trying to sell me on the depth of the interior line. I'm still in wait-and-see mode. Let's see how they stop the run. Still have little belief they'll be able to get to the QB consistently. It's mostly the same unit as last year and they didn't upgrade. Is Jordan van den Berg the truth? We're about to find out. He was fun to watch at camp. Let's see how he handles a counterpunch from the NFL.

T.J. Edwards, Devin Bush, D'Marco Jackson, Keyshaun Elliott

Norton: If there's a group almost certain to look different before Week 1, it's this one. Maybe Jack Sanborn comes back after some post-cutdown roster maneuvering.

Braggs: Easily the least talked about unit on the Bears on either side of the ball and definitely the unit that should be talked about more. They appear to have quality depth. TJ Edwards looks healthy. D'Marco Jackson looks empowered. And Devin Bush looks like a heat-seeking missile at times.

Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad II, Clark Phillips III, Josh Blackwell

Jahns: Smith appeared to be making a late push after missing part of camp with an injury. It included making two pass breakups in the Bears' preseason win against the Titans.

But the arrival of Phillips changed Smith's place on the team. Phillips has the versatility to play outside at cornerback and inside at nickel back, where Muhammad appears to be the starter as a rookie right now.

Hoge : Phillips was primarily an undersized outside corner in Atlanta so it will be interesting to see if the Bears have different plans for him. It's a shame Smith couldn't stay healthy because he certainly showed starting potential when he was able to play. Don't forget about Cam Lewis. If something were to happen to Johnson or Stevenson, they could kick Muhammad outside and put Lewis in the slot.

Braggs: This unit is cursed, plain and simple. Murphy's Law: anything that can go wrong will go wrong. I had a close eye on Jaylon Johnson during camp. He was getting beat quite a bit from my eyes against a tough Bears offense but it sounds like he had good showings in the joint practices. I think we need to have reasonable expectations for rookies starting on this defense, including Malik Muhammed who's already been asked to do so many things at camp with all the injuries to that group.

Dillon Thieneman, Cam Lewis, Xavier Woods, Elijah Hicks, Coby Bryant, Skyler Thomas

Jahns: This feels like a position that changes often this season as the Bears try to make up for the loss of Bryant. That could mean the competition between Lewis, Woods and Hicks continues into the season. Or it could mean that other players are added to the mix.

Carman: Is Thieneman ready to be a No. 1 safety? Logic tells me no. At least he will have veteran leadership around him to help him progress. This is one of the weaker safety rooms in the league with Coby Bryant out.

Hoge : Where would this room be if Thieneman didn't fall to No. 25? The Bears really need him to be in the defensive rookie of the year conversation.

Braggs: I thought Thieneman finished camp strong. His play recognition started to speed up and he started to get in some windows. Next step? Trusting your eyes and taking away the football. I was hopeful Cam Lewis could be what Kalif Raymond is to the offense. And he could still be that, but with the injury to Bryant, it feels like he won't be able to thrive as a smaller role guy and now will be asked for bigger responsibilities.

Kicker Cairo Santos, punter Tory Taylor, long snapper Beau Gardner

Carman: Does Beau know long snapping? The Bears don't seem sold that he does. I don't think there is much room for error for the rookie. Taylor had an improved preseason. Will it translate? Santos distance seems to have gained a yard or three.

articles.title: Reds/Cubs Sunday Night Baseball game to begin in rain delay
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Reds are set to wrap their weekend series in Wrigley Field against the Chicago Cubs on Sunday night. They're even going to have Joey Votto in the building as an on-field analyst seeing as the game is being carried nationally on both NBC and Peacock as the featured Sunday Night Baseball game of the week.

Unfortunately, it appears the game won't be starting on-time at 7:20 PM ET.

As veteran ESPN reporter Jesse Rogers relayed shortly after 6:40 PM ET, the game's going to be delayed due to rain in the Chicago area.

Just how long we'll have to wait before Shota Imanaga throws the game's first pitch remains to be seen.

What also becomes interesting is what impact this will have on Reds starter Chase Burns. He was already expected to begin seeing his total pitch counts reduced as a way of managing the load of getting through the entire season as a starter, and obviously having to stay warm for longer before even beginning the game could mean his already expected-to-be short night could end up even shorter.

articles.title: Seahawks 2026 roster cuts: Seattle waives both rookie cornerback draft picks
articles.summary: The Seahawks have waived Andre Fuller in addition to Michael Dansby.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks have opted to keep neither of their seventh-round rookie cornerbacks on the initial 53-man roster.

ESPN's Brady Henderson reported that former Toledo corner Andre Fuller, who was drafted alongside former Arizona standout Michael Dansby, has been waived. Dansby was also waived by the team. If both clear waivers come Monday, then they could return via the practice squad.

Seattle's cornerback room post-Riq Woolen appears to be constantly fluctuating outside of Josh Jobe, Devon Witherspoon, and Nehemiah Pritchett. The team drafted Julian Neal in the third round, although he missed all of preseason with an injury, while Fuller and Dansby got extensive preseason work. Seattle also signed Terrion Arnold ( who likely won't be around any time soon ) and veteran Trevon Diggs, as well as traded for rookie cornerback Avery Smith from the Los Angeles Chargers . We shall see if another veteran corner in Noah Igbinoghene made the roster, or if he ends up getting released (and potentially put on the practice squad).

Unless Deven Eastern is an unexpected inclusion, none of Seattle's sixth- or seventh-rounders from this year's draft will have made the 53-man roster. It's not too much of a surprise given the perceived weakness of this year's draft as a whole.
